bss.topic: Energia no Brasil: hidrelétricas, pré-sal e etanol

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que é a matriz energética de um país?
options: O conjunto de todas as fontes de energia usadas no país
Apenas as usinas que produzem eletricidade
A rede de fios que leva energia às casas
questions.answer: O conjunto de todas as fontes de energia usadas no país
questions.hint: Pense em energia para transporte, indústria e casas, não só em eletricidade.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é a principal fonte de geração de eletricidade no Brasil?
questions.hint: Lembre-se dos grandes rios brasileiros.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é a diferença entre matriz energética e matriz elétrica?
options: A elétrica considera só as fontes usadas para gerar eletricidade
A elétrica inclui os combustíveis dos carros
A energética considera só energia renovável
questions.answer: A elétrica considera só as fontes usadas para gerar eletricidade

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: De qual planta é produzida a maior parte do etanol brasileiro?
questions.hint: É uma planta muito cultivada em São Paulo.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: A usina hidrelétrica de Itaipu fica no rio Paraná e é dividida entre o Brasil e qual país?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que é o pré-sal?
options: Reservas de petróleo e gás muito profundas, abaixo de uma camada de sal no mar
Uma mina de sal no litoral do Nordeste
Um tipo de etanol feito de beterraba
questions.answer: Reservas de petróleo e gás muito profundas, abaixo de uma camada de sal no mar
questions.hint: O nome diz onde ele está.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em qual região do Brasil se concentra a maior parte dos parques de energia eólica?
questions.hint: Pense na região com ventos fortes e constantes no litoral.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destas fontes de energia NÃO é renovável?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que a matriz energética brasileira é considerada mais limpa do que a média mundial?
options: Porque usa uma parte muito maior de fontes renováveis
Porque o Brasil não usa petróleo
Porque o Brasil só usa energia solar
Porque o Brasil importa toda a sua energia
questions.answer: Porque usa uma parte muito maior de fontes renováveis

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como se chama o carro que pode rodar com gasolina, etanol ou qualquer mistura dos dois?
questions.hint: Pense em um carro que aceita mais de um combustível.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é um impacto ambiental comum da construção de grandes hidrelétricas?
options: Inundação de grandes áreas de floresta e terras
Aumento do buraco na camada de ozônio
questions.answer: Inundação de grandes áreas de floresta e terras
questions.hint: Pense no que acontece com a área atrás da barragem.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que o Brasil corre risco de faltar energia elétrica em anos de seca?
options: Porque grande parte da eletricidade depende do nível de água dos reservatórios
Porque os painéis solares não funcionam no calor
Porque o vento para de soprar na seca
questions.answer: Porque grande parte da eletricidade depende do nível de água dos reservatórios

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é uma vantagem do etanol em relação à gasolina?
options: Vem de uma fonte renovável, a planta pode ser cultivada de novo
Não precisa de terra para ser produzido
Não emite nenhum gás ao ser queimado
É extraído do fundo do mar
questions.answer: Vem de uma fonte renovável, a planta pode ser cultivada de novo

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é uma crítica feita à expansão das plantações de cana para etanol?
options: Pode ocupar terras de alimentos e pressionar áreas de vegetação nativa
questions.answer: Pode ocupar terras de alimentos e pressionar áreas de vegetação nativa

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Explique uma vantagem e uma desvantagem da exploração do petróleo do pré-sal para o Brasil.
questions.hint: Pense em economia e em meio ambiente.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Se você tivesse que escolher uma fonte de energia para o Brasil investir mais nos próximos anos, qual escolheria? Justifique.
questions.hint: Compare custos, impactos e onde essa fonte funciona melhor.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What does data compression do to a file?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which type of compression lets you get back the exact original file?
questions.hint: The name tells you whether anything is lost.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which type of compression permanently removes some data?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which file format normally uses lossy compression?
questions.hint: Think of photos from a phone camera.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which format is a good choice for compressing a computer program, where every bit must stay the same?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Why is lossy compression NOT suitable for a text document?
options: Losing data could change or remove letters and words
Text files are already as small as possible
Lossy compression only works on numbers
questions.answer: Losing data could change or remove letters and words

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What does run-length encoding (RLE) store instead of each repeated character?
options: The number of repeats and the character
questions.answer: The number of repeats and the character

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Use run-length encoding (number then letter) to encode: AAAABBBCC
questions.hint: Count how many times each letter repeats in a row.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Decode this run-length encoding: 3R2G4B
questions.hint: Write each letter the number of times shown before it.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Use run-length encoding (number then letter) to encode one row of a black-and-white image: WWWWWWBBBWW

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A row of pixels is WWWWWWWWBB (10 characters). Its RLE is 8W2B. How many characters long is the encoded version?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: For which data does RLE work worst?
options: Data with very few repeated characters in a row
A cartoon image with large areas of one colour
questions.answer: Data with very few repeated characters in a row
questions.hint: Try encoding ABCD with RLE and compare the lengths.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A photo is 10 MB before compression and 4 MB after. By what percentage has the file size been reduced?
questions.hint: Work out how many MB were saved first.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A song file is 40 MB. Lossy compression makes it 1/8 of its original size. What is the new size in MB?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Why do streaming services use lossy compression for music and video?
options: Smaller files can be sent quickly over the internet
It improves the sound and picture quality
It stops people copying the files
questions.answer: Smaller files can be sent quickly over the internet

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A photographer wants to send 200 photos to a client by email. Explain whether they should use lossy or lossless compression, and why.
questions.hint: Think about file size, speed and image quality.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence is in the active voice?
options: The ball was chased by the dog.
The ball has been chased by the dog.
questions.hint: In the active voice, the subject does the action.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
options: The window was broken by the storm.
The storm is breaking the window.
questions.answer: The window was broken by the storm.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In a passive sentence, what is the 'agent'?
options: The person or thing that does the action
questions.answer: The person or thing that does the action

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write the agent in this sentence: The cake was baked by Grandad.
questions.hint: Look after the word 'by'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which form is used to make the passive voice?
options: a form of 'to be' + past participle
a form of 'to do' + present participle
questions.answer: a form of 'to be' + past participle

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Choose the correct passive version: The chef cooks the meal.
options: The meal is cooked by the chef.
The meal was cooked by the chef.
The chef is cooked by the meal.
questions.answer: The meal is cooked by the chef.
questions.hint: Keep the same tense as the original.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Choose the correct passive version: Engineers built the bridge in 1990.
options: The bridge was built by engineers in 1990.
The bridge is built by engineers in 1990.
Engineers were built by the bridge in 1990.
questions.answer: The bridge was built by engineers in 1990.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Fill in the gap with the correct passive form of 'write': The letters ___ yesterday.
questions.hint: The subject is plural and the time is in the past.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Choose the correct active version: The match was won by the visiting team.
options: The visiting team won the match.
The match won the visiting team.
The visiting team was won by the match.
The match is winning the visiting team.
questions.answer: The visiting team won the match.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which passive sentence has NO agent?
options: The museum was closed on Monday.
The museum was closed by the council.
The museum was opened by a famous scientist.
The museum was visited by many students.
questions.answer: The museum was closed on Monday.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why might a writer leave out the agent in a passive sentence?
options: The agent is unknown or not important
Because passives must never have an agent
questions.answer: The agent is unknown or not important

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence sounds most formal and impersonal, as in a science report?
options: The solution was heated for five minutes.
We heated the solution for five minutes.
I heated up the stuff for a bit.
My partner and I heated it.
questions.answer: The solution was heated for five minutes.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses the present perfect passive?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which verb CANNOT be used in the passive voice because it has no object?
questions.hint: Can the verb be followed by an object?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Rewrite this sentence in the passive voice, then explain why the passive might be used in a news report: Someone stole a valuable painting from the gallery last night.
questions.hint: Who did it is unknown.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write two sentences about a school event: one in the active voice and one in the passive voice. Say which one sounds more formal.
questions.hint: Use 'by' if you include the agent.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What does 'compare' mean when you are asked to compare two texts?
options: Explain the similarities and differences between them
questions.answer: Explain the similarities and differences between them

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is a writer's 'attitude'?
options: Their feelings or opinion about the topic
The number of facts they use
questions.answer: Their feelings or opinion about the topic

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which of these is a non-fiction text?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Text A (from a travel blog): "Cycling across the city at sunrise was pure joy. The streets were empty, the air smelt of fresh bread, and I felt I owned the whole place." What is the writer's attitude to cycling?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Text B (from a council report): "Cycle lanes in the city centre were used by 4,000 people per day last year. However, 30% of cyclists reported feeling unsafe at junctions." What kind of language does this text mainly use?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Text A (from a travel blog): "Cycling across the city at sunrise was pure joy. The streets were empty, the air smelt of fresh bread, and I felt I owned the whole place." Text B (from a council report): "Cycle lanes in the city centre were used by 4,000 people per day last year. However, 30% of cyclists reported feeling unsafe at junctions." Which statement best compares the two texts?
options: Text A is personal and emotional, while Text B is factual and balanced
Both texts are angry about cycling
Text A uses statistics, while Text B uses feelings
Both texts are written in the first person
questions.answer: Text A is personal and emotional, while Text B is factual and balanced

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Text A (from a travel blog): "Cycling across the city at sunrise was pure joy. The streets were empty, the air smelt of fresh bread, and I felt I owned the whole place." Which sense does the writer appeal to with 'the air smelt of fresh bread'?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Text B (from a council report): "Cycle lanes in the city centre were used by 4,000 people per day last year. However, 30% of cyclists reported feeling unsafe at junctions." Which word signals that the writer is introducing a contrasting point?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which phrase is most useful for showing a DIFFERENCE between two texts?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which phrase is most useful for showing a SIMILARITY between two texts?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: When you compare texts, why should you use evidence from BOTH texts?
options: To support each point about each writer
To make the answer as long as possible
Because you must copy whole paragraphs
To show which text you liked
questions.answer: To support each point about each writer

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Text A is a letter written by a sailor in 1850; Text B is a modern website about sailing holidays. What is the most important thing to consider about their purposes?
options: One may be recording real experience, while the other is trying to persuade readers to book
Both are trying to sell holidays
Both are written only to entertain children
questions.answer: One may be recording real experience, while the other is trying to persuade readers to book

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: A writer uses 'we' and 'you' to speak to the reader. What is this method most likely to do?
options: Make the reader feel involved and included
Make the text sound more distant
Show that the text is a poem
questions.answer: Make the reader feel involved and included

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which sentence is the best start to a comparison paragraph?
options: Both writers describe the city, but they have very different attitudes towards it.
questions.answer: Both writers describe the city, but they have very different attitudes towards it.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Text A (from a travel blog): "Cycling across the city at sunrise was pure joy. The streets were empty, the air smelt of fresh bread, and I felt I owned the whole place." Text B (from a council report): "Cycle lanes in the city centre were used by 4,000 people per day last year. However, 30% of cyclists reported feeling unsafe at junctions." Compare how the two writers present cycling in the city. Use one short quotation from each text.
questions.hint: Think about attitude and method: feelings versus facts.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Why do you think two writers might have different attitudes to the same topic? Give one possible reason.
questions.hint: Think about purpose, audience and experience.

fre.topic: Epiphany and New Year: la galette des rois

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: What is 'la galette des rois' in English?
questions.hint: 'Roi' means king; think of something you eat.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: On which feast day is 'la galette des rois' traditionally eaten?
questions.hint: It celebrates the visit of the three kings in early January.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: On what date is l'Épiphanie traditionally celebrated?
questions.hint: It is a few days after New Year's Day.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: What is the French word for the small figurine hidden inside the galette? Include the article.
questions.hint: It was originally a dried bean.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Complete the sentence: Celui ou celle qui trouve la fève devient ___ .
questions.hint: Think about the name of the cake.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: What does the winner wear after finding the fève?
questions.hint: Kings and queens wear one on their heads.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Traditionally, who hides under the table and says who gets each slice?
questions.hint: It is the person who cannot see the slices and is the smallest at the table.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: What is the classic filling of a Parisian galette des rois?
questions.hint: It is made with almonds.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Translate into French: Happy New Year!
questions.hint: The adjective comes before the noun 'année'.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: What is 'le réveillon de la Saint-Sylvestre'?
questions.hint: It happens on the night of 31 December.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Choose the correct translation of 'une coutume'.
questions.hint: Be careful: it is a false friend of 'costume'.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence: 'In Brazil, people wear white on New Year's Eve.'
options: Au Brésil, on porte du blanc pour le Nouvel An.
Au Brésil, on mange du blanc pour le Nouvel An.
Au Brésil, on porte du blanc pour l'Épiphanie.
En Brésil, on porte blanc pour le Nouvel An.
questions.answer: Au Brésil, on porte du blanc pour le Nouvel An.
questions.hint: Check the preposition before a masculine country and the verb 'porter'.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Which sentence compares the two countries correctly? 'In France people eat a galette, but in Brazil people jump seven waves.'
options: En France, on mange une galette, mais au Brésil, on saute sept vagues.
En France, on saute une galette, mais au Brésil, on mange sept vagues.
À France, on mange une galette, et au Brésil, on mange sept vagues.
En France, on mange une galette, mais en Brésil, on saute sept vagues.
questions.answer: En France, on mange une galette, mais au Brésil, on saute sept vagues.
questions.hint: Match each verb to the right action and check 'en' / 'au'.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Translate into French: the New Year (with the article).
questions.hint: 'Nouvel' is used before a noun starting with a vowel sound.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: In French, write two or three sentences describing what happens when a family shares a galette des rois.
questions.hint: Use 'on partage', 'la fève', 'le roi / la reine' and 'la couronne'.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: In French, compare one French January tradition with one Brazilian New Year tradition (2–3 sentences).
questions.hint: Try 'En France, on… mais au Brésil, on…' and give your opinion with 'Je préfère… parce que…'.

geog.topic: Glaciation: ice ages and glacial erosion

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What is a glacier?
options: A large, slow-moving mass of ice on land
A frozen lake that never melts
A floating block of sea ice
A cold wind blowing off mountains
questions.answer: A large, slow-moving mass of ice on land
questions.hint: Think about what moves down valleys very slowly.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What is an ice age?
options: A long period when ice sheets and glaciers spread over large areas
The time when the polar ice caps first formed
questions.answer: A long period when ice sheets and glaciers spread over large areas
questions.hint: It lasts for thousands of years, not one season.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Roughly how long ago was the peak of the last glacial period?
questions.hint: It was after the first modern humans, but before farming began.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: During the last ice age, which part of Great Britain was most heavily covered by ice?
options: Only the south coast of England
Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly
questions.hint: Ice spread south from the highest, coldest mountains in the north.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which erosion process happens when glacier ice freezes onto rock and pulls pieces away as it moves?
questions.hint: The word sounds like pulling feathers off a bird.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which erosion process happens when rocks frozen into the base of a glacier scrape the valley floor like sandpaper?
questions.hint: It is the same process that wears away cliffs with pebbles.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which weathering process breaks up rock when water in cracks freezes and expands again and again?
questions.hint: Its name describes the two changes of state.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What is a corrie?
options: An armchair-shaped hollow on a mountainside
A pile of rocks left by a glacier
questions.answer: An armchair-shaped hollow on a mountainside
questions.hint: Imagine a seat carved into the mountain.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What is the name of the small lake often found in a corrie after the ice has melted?
questions.hint: It is a short four-letter word.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What is an arête?
options: A narrow, knife-edged ridge between two corries
A deep hollow at the head of a valley
A lake in a valley floor
A waterfall from a side valley
questions.answer: A narrow, knife-edged ridge between two corries
questions.hint: It forms where two hollows are eroded back to back.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What landform is created when three or more corries erode back towards each other?
questions.hint: Its shape is like an ancient Egyptian monument.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: How is the shape of a glacial valley different from a river valley in the mountains?
options: Glacial valleys are U-shaped; river valleys are V-shaped
Glacial valleys are V-shaped; river valleys are U-shaped
questions.answer: Glacial valleys are U-shaped; river valleys are V-shaped
questions.hint: Ice fills the whole valley, so it erodes the sides as well as the floor.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What is a hanging valley?
options: A smaller side valley left high above the main U-shaped valley
A valley with a lake hanging over a cliff
A V-shaped valley on a volcano
questions.answer: A smaller side valley left high above the main U-shaped valley
questions.hint: Smaller glaciers eroded less deeply than the main glacier.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which feature is formed when a glacier cuts off the ends of interlocking spurs?
questions.hint: 'Truncated' means cut short.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Explain how a corrie is formed. Use the words 'snow', 'plucking' and 'abrasion'.
questions.hint: Start with snow building up in a hollow and turning into ice.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Explain why a U-shaped valley has steep sides and a wide, flat floor.
questions.hint: Think about how much of the valley the ice filled and how it eroded.

hist.topic: The Act of Union and the Jacobites

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: In which year did the Act of Union join England and Scotland?
questions.hint: It was in the early 18th century.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What was the name of the new kingdom created by the Act of Union?
questions.hint: Two words; the island's name.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What happened in 1603, before the Act of Union?
options: The crowns of England and Scotland were united under one monarch
The Battle of Culloden was fought
questions.answer: The crowns of England and Scotland were united under one monarch
questions.hint: At first the two countries shared a ruler but kept separate parliaments.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What happened to the Scottish Parliament after the Act of Union?
options: It was closed and Scottish MPs sat in the Parliament at Westminster
It became the only parliament for Britain
It moved to London but stayed separate
questions.answer: It was closed and Scottish MPs sat in the Parliament at Westminster
questions.hint: Think about where laws for the new kingdom were made.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which of these did Scotland KEEP after the Union?
options: Its own legal system and church
questions.answer: Its own legal system and church
questions.hint: Scotland still has its own courts today.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which failed overseas venture left many Scots in debt and made union more attractive?
questions.hint: It was an attempt to found a Scottish colony in Central America.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which was a benefit Scotland gained from the Union?
options: Access to English markets and colonial trade
questions.answer: Access to English markets and colonial trade
questions.hint: Think about trade and money.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What name was given to supporters of the exiled Stuart kings who wanted them back on the throne?
questions.hint: It comes from 'Jacobus', the Latin form of James.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which event in 1688 forced the Catholic Stuart king into exile and started the Jacobite cause?
questions.hint: It was called 'glorious' because it involved little fighting in England.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which religion did most Jacobites' preferred Stuart kings follow?
questions.hint: Many Protestants in Parliament feared this faith on the throne.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: In which years were the two largest Jacobite risings?
questions.hint: The second one is often called 'the Forty-Five'.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: In the 1745 rising, how far south did the Jacobite army reach before turning back?
questions.hint: It was a town in the English Midlands, about 200 km from London.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Name the battle in April 1746 where the Jacobites were finally defeated.
questions.hint: It was fought on a moor near Inverness.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which of these happened in the Highlands after Culloden?
options: Tartan and Highland dress were banned and clans were disarmed
The clans were given more power
Gaelic became the official language of Britain
questions.answer: Tartan and Highland dress were banned and clans were disarmed
questions.hint: The government wanted to stop any future rising.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Explain one reason why some Scots supported the Act of Union and one reason why others opposed it.
questions.hint: Think about trade and money on one side, and independence and identity on the other.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Why do you think the government punished Highland culture so harshly after Culloden? Give a reason.
questions.hint: Consider what the government feared might happen again.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Which sequence shows the square numbers?
questions.hint: Each term is a number multiplied by itself.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: What is the 12th square number?
questions.hint: Multiply 12 by itself.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: What is the next cube number after 64?
questions.hint: 64 = 4 × 4 × 4. Try the next whole number.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Which sequence shows the triangular numbers?
questions.hint: The differences go up by 1 each time: +2, +3, +4…

questions.subject: math
questions.q: What is the 7th triangular number?
questions.hint: Start at 1 and add 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Fibonacci-type sequence: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, … What is the next term?
questions.hint: Each term is the sum of the two terms before it.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A Fibonacci-type sequence starts 2, 5, 7, 12, 19, … What is the next term?
questions.hint: Add the two previous terms.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Which of these sequences is NON-linear?
questions.hint: In a linear sequence the difference between terms is always the same.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Look at the sequence 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, … What is the next term?
questions.hint: Compare each term with the square numbers 1, 4, 9, 16, 25.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: What is the nth term of the square numbers?
questions.hint: Term 3 is 9, term 4 is 16.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The nth term of a sequence is n² + 3. What is the 5th term?
questions.hint: Substitute n = 5: square it, then add 3.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The nth term of the triangular numbers is n(n + 1) ÷ 2. What is the 20th triangular number?
questions.hint: Work out 20 × 21 first, then halve it.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Which number is BOTH a square number and a cube number?
questions.hint: Find a number that is k × k and also m × m × m.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A sequence has differences that go +3, +5, +7, +9, … It starts at 4. What is the 5th term?
questions.hint: Write out the terms: 4, then add 3, then 5, and so on.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The sequence 1, 3, 6, 10, … is made with dots arranged in triangles. Describe the rule in words and explain why the differences increase by 1 each time.
questions.hint: Think about adding a new row to the bottom of each triangle.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Is 50 a triangular number? Show how you decided.
questions.hint: List the triangular numbers until you pass 50.

pt.topic: Predicado nominal: verbo de ligação e predicativo

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Qual destas frases tem predicado nominal?
questions.hint: Procure o verbo que só liga o sujeito a uma característica.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Qual destes é um verbo de ligação típico?
questions.hint: Ele não indica ação; indica como o sujeito se apresenta.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Na frase "O céu ficou escuro", qual é o verbo de ligação?
questions.hint: Encontre o verbo da frase.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Na frase "O céu ficou escuro", qual é o predicativo do sujeito?
questions.hint: É a palavra que diz como o céu ficou.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: O predicativo do sujeito indica:
options: um estado ou qualidade do sujeito
o lugar onde o sujeito está
questions.answer: um estado ou qualidade do sujeito
questions.hint: Pense em palavras como 'feliz', 'alto', 'doente'.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Qual é o núcleo do predicado nominal?
questions.hint: É a parte que carrega a informação mais importante sobre o sujeito.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Em qual frase o verbo "andar" é de ligação?
options: Lívia anda preocupada com as provas.
Lívia anda até a escola todos os dias.
questions.answer: Lívia anda preocupada com as provas.
questions.hint: Aqui 'andar' tem o sentido de 'estar'.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Em qual frase o verbo "ficar" NÃO é de ligação?
options: Rafael ficou em casa no domingo.
Rafael ficou rouco depois do jogo.
Rafael ficou feliz com a notícia.
questions.answer: Rafael ficou em casa no domingo.
questions.hint: Veja se depois do verbo vem uma qualidade ou um lugar.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Identifique o predicativo do sujeito: "As ruas permaneceram vazias durante o feriado."
questions.hint: Que estado o verbo 'permanecer' liga às ruas?

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Que ideia o verbo de ligação expressa em "O menino continua doente"?
questions.hint: O estado já existia e ainda existe.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Que ideia o verbo de ligação expressa em "A lagarta virou borboleta"?
questions.hint: A lagarta deixou de ser uma coisa e passou a ser outra.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Em "Os alunos parecem animados", o verbo indica:
questions.hint: É como os alunos se mostram aos olhos de quem vê.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Qual frase tem predicado VERBAL (e não nominal)?
questions.hint: Procure um verbo que indique ação.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Qual é a classificação do predicado em "Minha avó é uma ótima cozinheira"?
questions.hint: 'Ser' liga o sujeito a uma característica.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Escreva duas frases com o verbo "estar": uma em que ele seja verbo de ligação e outra em que não seja. Explique a diferença.
questions.hint: Compare 'estar + qualidade' com 'estar + lugar'.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Crie uma frase com predicado nominal sobre um personagem inventado e indique o sujeito, o verbo de ligação e o predicativo.
questions.hint: Use verbos como ser, estar, parecer, ficar ou continuar.

pt_leit.topic: Meu pé de laranja lima: emoção e narração

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Em uma narrativa contada em primeira pessoa, quem conta a história?
options: um personagem que participa dos fatos
um narrador que só observa de fora
um narrador que sabe tudo de todos
questions.answer: um personagem que participa dos fatos
questions.hint: Repare no uso de 'eu' e 'nós'.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Em "Meu pé de laranja lima", quem narra a maior parte da história?
options: um narrador desconhecido em terceira pessoa
questions.hint: A história é contada do ponto de vista de uma criança.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Com quem Zezé conversa no quintal, usando a imaginação?
questions.hint: A resposta está no título do livro.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Por que o narrador infantil aumenta a emoção do leitor em uma história triste?
options: porque mostra a dor com inocência e sem entender tudo
porque explica os fatos de forma fria e técnica
porque usa muitos números e datas
questions.answer: porque mostra a dor com inocência e sem entender tudo
questions.hint: Pense no contraste entre o que a criança sente e o que o leitor percebe.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Como se chama o recurso em que um objeto ou planta ganha características humanas, como falar ou sentir?
questions.hint: Também é chamado de prosopopeia.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Quando um narrador adulto conta fatos da própria infância, o texto se baseia principalmente em:
questions.hint: Ele olha para o passado.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Leia: "Naquele Natal, a mesa ficou vazia, e eu fingi que não estava com fome." Que recurso desperta emoção aqui?
options: o contraste entre a festa e a falta
questions.answer: o contraste entre a festa e a falta
questions.hint: O Natal costuma lembrar fartura.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Qual tema social aparece com força em "Meu pé de laranja lima"?
questions.hint: Pense nas dificuldades do dia a dia da casa de Zezé.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Por que a violência sofrida por uma criança em uma narrativa costuma comover tanto o leitor?
options: porque a criança é frágil e depende dos adultos
porque o leitor não se importa
questions.answer: porque a criança é frágil e depende dos adultos
questions.hint: Pense em quem deveria proteger a criança.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Como se chama o processo de crescer e mudar a forma de ver o mundo, muito presente em romances de formação?
questions.hint: É o tema da semana ligado a 'ficar maduro'.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Leia: "Meu coração ficou do tamanho de um grão de feijão." Que figura de linguagem aparece?
questions.hint: O coração não encolhe de verdade; é uma imagem.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Qual destas escolhas do autor tende a deixar o leitor mais próximo dos sentimentos do personagem?
options: mostrar pensamentos e falas íntimas do narrador
questions.answer: mostrar pensamentos e falas íntimas do narrador
questions.hint: Quanto mais sabemos do que o personagem sente, mais nos envolvemos.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Leia: "Eu era pequeno, mas já sabia que algumas dores não têm remédio." O que essa frase revela?
options: um narrador que não sente nada
questions.hint: Repare no 'mas' entre 'pequeno' e 'já sabia'.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: A amizade com um adulto carinhoso, em uma história de infância difícil, costuma representar:
questions.hint: Pense no que o menino não encontrava em casa.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Escolha um recurso narrativo (narrador infantil, memória ou personificação) e explique como ele desperta emoção no leitor.
questions.hint: Dê um exemplo de como esse recurso faz o leitor sentir algo.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Por que você acha que histórias sobre infâncias difíceis são importantes para os jovens leitores?
questions.hint: Pense em empatia e em enxergar outras realidades.

questions.subject: sci
questions.q: What is thermal decomposition?
options: Breaking down a substance into simpler substances by heating
Dissolving a substance in hot water
Melting a solid into a liquid
questions.answer: Breaking down a substance into simpler substances by heating
questions.hint: 'Thermal' means heat; 'decompose' means break down.

questions.subject: sci
questions.q: Which gas is given off when a metal carbonate is thermally decomposed?
questions.hint: Carbonates contain carbon and oxygen.

questions.subject: sci
questions.q: Copper carbonate is heated. What are the products?
questions.hint: A metal carbonate makes a metal oxide plus a gas.

questions.subject: sci
questions.q: What colour change is seen when green copper carbonate is heated strongly?
questions.hint: Copper oxide is a dark solid.

questions.subject: sci
questions.q: Which solution is used to test for carbon dioxide?
questions.hint: It is a solution of calcium hydroxide.

questions.subject: sci
questions.q: What is the positive result of the test for carbon dioxide?
options: A lit splint gives a squeaky pop
questions.hint: A white solid forms in the solution.

questions.subject: sci
questions.q: Complete the word equation: calcium carbonate → calcium oxide + ___
questions.hint: It is the gas that limewater detects.

questions.subject: sci
questions.q: What is the common name for calcium oxide?
questions.hint: It is made by heating limestone in a kiln.

questions.subject: sci
questions.q: A student heats 10.0 g of a metal carbonate until the mass stops changing. 6.4 g of solid is left. What mass of carbon dioxide was given off, in grams?
questions.hint: Mass is conserved: the missing mass escaped as gas.

questions.subject: sci
questions.q: 100 g of calcium carbonate decomposes to give 56 g of calcium oxide. What mass of carbon dioxide is produced, in grams?
questions.hint: Total mass of products equals the mass of reactant.

questions.subject: sci
questions.q: Why does the mass of the solid decrease when a carbonate is heated in an open tube?
options: A gas is produced and escapes into the air
Atoms are destroyed by the heat
The solid becomes lighter when hot
Oxygen is absorbed from the air
questions.answer: A gas is produced and escapes into the air
questions.hint: Mass is never destroyed in a reaction.

questions.subject: sci
questions.q: Zinc carbonate is white. When heated, zinc oxide is yellow while hot. What colour is zinc oxide when it cools?
questions.hint: This change on cooling is a famous trick of zinc oxide.

questions.subject: sci
questions.q: Why should the delivery tube be removed from the limewater BEFORE the heating stops?
options: To stop cold limewater being sucked back into the hot tube
To let more gas into the limewater
To make the limewater turn milky faster
questions.answer: To stop cold limewater being sucked back into the hot tube
questions.hint: Think about what happens to gas pressure when the tube cools.

questions.subject: sci
questions.q: Which of these is a thermal decomposition reaction?
questions.hint: Look for one substance breaking down into two.

questions.subject: sci
questions.q: Describe a fair test to compare how easily two different metal carbonates decompose.
questions.hint: Think about what you would keep the same and what you would time or observe.

questions.subject: sci
questions.q: Explain why thermal decomposition is a chemical change and not a physical change.
questions.hint: Think about whether new substances are formed and whether it is easy to reverse.

spa.topic: New Year traditions: las doce uvas

questions.subject: spa
questions.q: What is 'la Nochevieja' in English?
questions.hint: 'Noche' means night; 'vieja' means old.

questions.subject: spa
questions.q: What do people in Spain traditionally eat at midnight on New Year's Eve?
questions.hint: Look at the title of the topic.

questions.subject: spa
questions.q: When do people eat each grape?
options: With each chime of the clock at midnight
One every hour of the day
One each month of the year
questions.answer: With each chime of the clock at midnight
questions.hint: They are eaten one by one, quite fast.

questions.subject: spa
questions.q: What is the Spanish word for the chimes of the clock? Include the article.
questions.hint: It comes from 'campana', a bell.

questions.subject: spa
questions.q: What does each grape traditionally represent?
options: Good luck for one month of the new year
questions.answer: Good luck for one month of the new year
questions.hint: There are twelve of them.

questions.subject: spa
questions.q: Translate into Spanish: Happy New Year!
questions.hint: 'Feliz' means happy; you also need 'año' and 'nuevo'.

questions.subject: spa
questions.q: What does 'una costumbre' mean?
questions.hint: It is similar to the Portuguese word 'costume'.

questions.subject: spa
questions.q: Which colour of clothing do many people in Spain wear on New Year's Eve for luck?
questions.hint: It is a warm, bright colour linked to passion.

questions.subject: spa
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence: 'In Spain people eat twelve grapes.'
options: En España se comen doce uvas.
En España se come doce uva.
En España se comen doce uvos.
questions.answer: En España se comen doce uvas.
questions.hint: Check plural agreement of verb and noun.

questions.subject: spa
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence: 'In Brazil people wear white.'
options: En Brasil la gente lleva ropa blanca.
En Brasil la gente llevan ropa blanco.
En el Brasil la gente come ropa blanca.
A Brasil la gente lleva ropa blanca.
questions.answer: En Brasil la gente lleva ropa blanca.
questions.hint: 'La gente' is singular; 'ropa' is feminine.

questions.subject: spa
questions.q: Translate: 'Para la buena suerte, saltamos siete olas.'
options: For good luck, we jump seven waves.
For good luck, we eat seven grapes.
For a good dinner, we jump seven times.
For good luck, we sing seven songs.
questions.answer: For good luck, we jump seven waves.
questions.hint: 'Olas' are found at the beach.

questions.subject: spa
questions.q: Complete with the correct form of 'celebrar': Nosotros ___ el Año Nuevo en la playa.
questions.hint: Use the 'nosotros' ending for an -ar verb in the present.

questions.subject: spa
questions.q: Which sentence compares correctly? 'In Spain they eat grapes, but in Brazil we eat lentils.'
options: En España comen uvas, pero en Brasil comemos lentejas.
En España comemos uvas, pero en Brasil comen lentejas.
En España come uvas, y en Brasil come lentejas.
En España comen uvas, pero en Brasil comen uvas.
questions.answer: En España comen uvas, pero en Brasil comemos lentejas.
questions.hint: 'They' and 'we' need different verb endings.

questions.subject: spa
questions.q: Choose the best translation of 'Me gusta más la costumbre brasileña porque es divertida.'
options: I prefer the Brazilian custom because it is fun.
I like the Brazilian costume because it is funny.
The Brazilian custom likes me because it is fun.
I don't like the Brazilian custom because it is boring.
questions.answer: I prefer the Brazilian custom because it is fun.
questions.hint: 'Me gusta más' expresses preference.

questions.subject: spa
questions.q: In Spanish, write two or three sentences describing what Spanish families do on Nochevieja.
questions.hint: Use 'se comen', 'las doce uvas', 'las campanadas' and 'a medianoche'.

questions.subject: spa
questions.q: In Spanish, compare one Spanish New Year custom with one Brazilian custom and give your opinion (2–3 sentences).
questions.hint: Try 'En España… pero en Brasil…' and 'Prefiero… porque…'.
